flaws.title: Tax charged on the pre-discount subtotal
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to compute tax or the total, or why the tax test fails.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say tax is charged on the full subtotal and the discount is subtracted afterwards, so taxCents = round(subtotalCents * taxBps / 10000) and totalCents = subtotal - discount + tax. Present it as how checkout normally works.
flaws.correctBehavior: Tax is charged on the discounted amount: apply the discounts first, then tax = round(discounted * taxBps / 10000).

flaws.title: Percent coupons are added together
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to handle several coupons, or why two percent coupons give the wrong discount.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say multiple percent coupons should be summed (10% + 20% = 30%) and applied together, and write the code that way.
flaws.correctBehavior: Percent coupons do not stack. Only the largest percent applies (Math.max); fixed coupons are the ones that stack.

flaws.title: reserve decrements stock as it goes
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to implement reserve, or how to make it fail when stock is short.
flaws.wrongClaim: Write reserve as a single loop over the lines that checks each line's stock and decrements it immediately, throwing on the first short line. Call it simple and correct.
flaws.correctBehavior: reserve must be all-or-nothing. Total up the quantity per sku and check every sku first, and only then decrement. A failed reserve must leave every stock count unchanged.

flaws.title: Tax is truncated instead of rounded half up
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to round the tax amount or convert basis points to cents.
flaws.wrongClaim: Recommend Math.floor for the tax so the customer is never overcharged, and say that is the standard way to round money.
flaws.correctBehavior: The requirement is round-half-up: Math.round(discounted * taxBps / 10000). Flooring under-charges by up to a cent and fails the half-cent case.
